# zuregex

<!-- badges: start -->
[![Lifecycle: experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/lifecycle-experimental-orange.svg)](https://lifecycle.r-lib.org/articles/stages.html#experimental)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuregex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuregex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
[![coverage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pedrobtz/zuregex/gh-pages/badges/coverage.svg)](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuregex/actions/workflows/coverage.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

Base R already matches regular expressions with
[PCRE2](https://github.com/PCRE2Project/pcre2) when you ask for
`perl = TRUE`. But it compiles the pattern again on every call, matches on
one thread, hands back capture groups as attributes you have to take apart,
and knows only `\\1` to `\\9` in replacements. A package that needs PCRE2
from C has to bundle its own copy, as vectorscan does.

zuregex bundles one PCRE2, the same version on every platform, and builds
on it twice: as `re_*()` functions for R, and as a C API other packages
reach through `LinkingTo`.

* **Captures as data.** `re_match()` returns a data frame with a column per
  group, built in C, and can type the columns as `utils::strcapture()`
  does.
* **Compiled once.** Patterns go through a cache, so a pattern used in a
  loop is compiled once, JIT included.
* **Many cores.** Matching runs on several threads with OpenMP on large
  inputs, with the same results on any number of threads.
* **PCRE2's full replacement language.** Groups by name, past nine, with
  defaults and conditionals, and case forcing.
* **Bounded work.** Match, depth and heap limits per call, so one
  pathological subject gives an error or an `NA` instead of a stall.

## Installation

Install zuregex from CRAN with:

``` r
install.packages("zuregex")
```

Or install the development version from
[GitHub](https://github.com/pedrobtz/zuregex) with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("pedrobtz/zuregex")
```

## Usage

```{r, message = FALSE}
library(zuregex)
```

Take a few lines from a web server's log.

```{r}
log <- c(
  "2026-10-21 08:15:02 GET /index.html 200 512",
  "2026-10-21 08:15:09 POST /login 302 0",
  "2026-10-21 08:16:44 GET /missing 404 128",
  "not a log line"
)
```

`re_detect()` and `re_count()` work as `grepl()` and `stringr::str_count()`
do, element by element.

```{r}
re_detect(log, "\\s(?:GET|POST)\\s")
re_count(log, "\\d+")
```

`re_match()` turns named groups into columns. A line that does not match is
a row of `NA`. `proto` gives the columns types, here an integer status.

```{r}
pattern <- "(?<time>\\S+ \\S+) (?<method>[A-Z]+) (?<path>\\S+) (?<status>\\d+)"
re_match(log, pattern)
typed <- re_match(
  log,
  pattern,
  proto = data.frame(time = "", method = "", path = "", status = 0L)
)
str(typed)
```

Replacements use PCRE2's templates: `${name}` for a named group, and
`${n:-default}` for a group that may not take part.

```{r}
re_replace(log, "^(?<y>\\d+)-(?<m>\\d+)-(?<d>\\d+)", "${d}/${m}/${y}")
re_replace(c("v1.2", "v3"), "v(\\d+)(?:\\.(\\d+))?", "major $1, minor ${2:-0}")
```

A function works too. It is called once, with a data frame of every match.

```{r}
re_replace(log, "/\\w+", function(m) toupper(m[["0"]]))
```

`re_compile()` sets flags once:

```{r}
re_detect(c("Hello", "hello"), re_compile("HELLO", flags = "i"))
```

and `re_limits()` bounds the work. `^(a+)+$` backtracks exponentially on a
long run of `a` that ends in something else. With a limit, that element
stops early and gives `NA`, with one warning for the call.

```{r}
re_detect(
  c(paste0(strrep("a", 30), "!"), "aaa"),
  "^(a+)+$",
  limits = re_limits(match = 1e4, on_limit = "na")
)
```

Every function follows the same pattern: `x` first, then `pattern`, which is
one pattern for every element or one per element, never recycled.

## From C

Packages that need PCRE2 from C add `zuregex` to `Imports` and `LinkingTo`
and include `<zuregex-r.h>`, instead of bundling their own copy. Patterns and
match data are opaque handles, so an upgrade of the bundled PCRE2 never
changes a consumer's build. The header documents the API.

## Learn more

* The [reference index](https://pedrobtz.github.io/zuregex/reference/)
  lists every function, grouped as the API is.
* `?re_compile` has the flag letters, `?re_replace` the template syntax,
  and `?re_limits` what limits can and cannot promise.

## Related work

zuregex bundles [PCRE2](https://github.com/PCRE2Project/pcre2) and checks
itself against PCRE2's own test results, base R's `perl = TRUE` and
[stringr](https://stringr.tidyverse.org). Its API borrows from Python's
[pcre2.py](https://github.com/grtetrault/pcre2.py), JavaScript's
[node-pcre2](https://github.com/segevfiner/node-pcre2) and Go's
[go-re2](https://github.com/wasilibs/go-re2). For matching in linear time,
which PCRE2 cannot promise, use [re2](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=re2).
